The Robertson Opus cultivates an urban oasis for luxury homes, dining and placemaking in District 9
article:
For years, Robertson Walk was a familiar dining and lifestyle destination along the Singapore River.

Now, The Robertson Opus is taking shape in its place, bringing new homes, retail offerings and landscaped public spaces to the Robertson Quay precinct in prime District 9.

Developed by Frasers Property and Sekisui House, the 999-year leasehold, mixed-use project will occupy the site of the former Robertson Walk commercial complex and the adjoining Fraser Place Robertson Walk serviced residence.

It will introduce 348 homes across five residential blocks arranged around a distinctive courtyard with publicly accessible spaces, alongside a retail podium that will retain the name Robertson Walk.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The project’s design also pays homage to the site’s heritage and the neighbourhood’s riverside character.

Its integration of residential, retail and communal spaces, with an emphasis on placemaking and sustainability, has earned it the Top Development title at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026.

“Our vision for The Robertson Opus was to deliver a distinctive riverside destination that combines quality homes, curated lifestyle offerings and meaningful communal spaces in one integrated environment,” says Tan Wee Hsien, CEO of Frasers Property Singapore.

He adds that the mixed-use project aims to enhance Robertson Quay’s vibrancy and create spaces “where people can live, connect and thrive”.

Prime riverside living with lasting appeal

Nestled between Fort Canning Hill and the Singapore River, The Robertson Opus is within walking distance of Robertson Quay’s restaurants, cafés and entertainment offerings.

Fort Canning, Clarke Quay and Great World MRT stations are nearby, while the Central Expressway provides road connectivity. Orchard Road and the CBD are also a short drive away.

Many buyers have been drawn to the 999-year leasehold tenure, prime riverside location and integrated lifestyle offerings.

“We have also seen interest from those seeking a legacy asset with generational appeal, as well as owner-occupiers who value the blend of city-centre convenience, wellness-focused amenities and proximity to the Singapore River’s vibrant lifestyle precinct,” Tan says.

Since its July 2025 debut, the project has attracted predominantly affluent Singaporeans, as well as permanent residents and a small number of international buyers.

The developers achieved a 41% take-up rate during the launch weekend, with 143 residential units sold at $3,360 psf on average. As at end-September 2026, about 60% of the residences had been sold.

“Homebuyers increasingly value developments that support their lifestyle, well-being and sense of belonging,” Tan notes.

Lively, connected community

The redevelopment presented an opportunity to reimagine the site while retaining the qualities that make the precinct unique.

Balancing renewal with respect for Robertson Quay’s character was a key consideration, Tan says.

The design thus prioritises openness, greenery and human-centric spaces. In terms of the architecture, modern facade compositions are harmonised with terracotta roof tiles and immersive landscaping.

Given the broader precinct’s history as a bustling waterfront trading corridor and gathering place, the developers applied a landscape framework that encourages interaction, connectivity and community engagement.

“Successful mixed-use developments are ultimately about placemaking,” Tan says.

“At The Robertson Opus, every component has been designed to complement one another while serving the needs of different user groups.”

Communal spaces are created to foster human connections and intergenerational engagement within a high-density urban environment. These include the Family Lawn, Gourmet Pavilion, Poolside Lounge, Reading Room, Children Sensory Garden and garden pavilions.

The project will also feature Singapore’s first sunken, privately owned public space, anchored by a three-storey green wall and water feature.

At the same time, the public-facing retail and dining promenade, along with strategically positioned internal public streets, contributes to the precinct’s vibrancy by extending the pedestrian experience.

This connects the development, riverfront and the surrounding neighbourhood, thereby merging the public and private realms.

The project will reintroduce Robertson Walk as an upscale destination with approximately 26 dining, retail and lifestyle units — catering to residents, visitors and the wider community.

“These complementary uses will foster a lively and engaging atmosphere, creating opportunities for meaningful social interaction and reinforcing Robertson Quay’s position as one of Singapore’s most sought-after lifestyle destinations,” Tan says.

Greenery, wellness and tranquillity

Extensive landscaping connects the residential blocks, elevated communal areas and retail podium.

The porous arrangement of the towers and the vertical internal courtyard — with cascading terraces, planted balconies and communal decks — draws breezes from the river deep into the development while mitigating heat build-up in the internal spaces.

Dense planting and water features also enable evaporative cooling and shading. More than 200 trees and 2,000 shrubs — comprising 40 to 50 native and regional species, including endangered trees — will be planted across the grounds.

Residents will benefit from a wellness-focused living environment that includes the rooftop Sky Forest with a 240m connected track across the blocks, as well as community gardening plots. Other amenities include a 45m lap pool, gym, sauna and social lounge.

“Together, these spaces support wellness, relaxation and social interaction while preserving the privacy and tranquillity of the residential experience,” Tan says.

The Robertson Opus has received BCA Green Mark GoldPlus certification. Sustainability measures include a climate-responsive design, naturally ventilated lobbies, low-volatile organic compound materials to improve indoor air quality, and rooftop solar photovoltaic panels.

Most of the existing carpark structure will be retained, while clay roof tiles and selected artefacts from the former development will be upcycled into an art wall at Level 1, preserving a link to the site’s past.

Meanwhile, the homes feature layouts that maximise usable space and natural ventilation.

Smaller unit types have ceiling heights of up to 3.2m, with built-in cabinetry making use of the additional height for storage. Strategically positioned windows encourage airflow, particularly in kitchens and bathrooms.

The unit interiors feature earthy tones and large-format tiles, and selected residences come with products from premium European brands such as Ernestomeda, Rimadesio and V-Zug.

With its rare 999-year tenure, luxury residences, tropical greenery and curated lifestyle offerings, The Robertson Opus brings together riverside living, wellness and community in the heart of District 9.

title: Newport Residences wins with elevated homes in a landmark CBD mixed-use development
article:
Newport Residences , City Developments Ltd ’s (CDL) ultra-luxury development on Anson Road in the CBD, launched for sale at the start of this year. The freehold project saw a healthy response, with buyers snapping up 57% of its 246 units during the Jan 31-Feb 1 launch weekend at an average price of $3,370 psf.

The robust performance reflected buyers’ anticipation for the project, which had been building up for some time. Newport Residences’ launch, originally scheduled for 2023, was postponed after the government raised additional buyer’s stamp duty (ABSD) rates as part of measures to cool the property market.

The ABSD hike, which kicked in near the end of April 2023, saw rates for foreigners — historically significant contributors to prime private home sales — double from 30% to 60%. Following the hike, foreign purchases of homes in the Core Central Region (CCR), typically seen as a proxy for luxury residences, took a hit, dampening the region’s sales.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

CDL’s decision to delay the launch of Newport Residences until 2026 has proven to be judicious, following a notable recovery in the CCR market over the past year. Post-launch, the project has continued to see steady sales, with caveats lodged to date indicating a take-up rate of roughly 80%.

The development also swept multiple honours at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026. At the awards ceremony on Oct 29, the project walked away with four titles: Design Excellence, Innovation Excellence, Marketing Excellence and Top Development.

Landmark mixed-use development

Newport Residences is part of Newport Plaza, a mixed-use development on the site of the former Fuji Xerox Towers office complex. Standing at 215m, the 45-storey Newport Plaza also houses Newport Tower, a collection of Grade A offices on Levels 2 to 9, and branded serviced apartments on Levels 10 to 22.

Newport Residences makes up the upper half of the tower, from Levels 23 to 45. Restaurants and a public square on Level 1 round out the tower’s offerings.

Currently under construction, Newport Plaza is set to become a striking centrepiece in downtown Singapore. The development’s components, stacked within a single skyscraper, create a “vertical town” that combines work, live and play functions in a cohesive environment, according to the development’s EPEA entry submission.

Newport Plaza will be connected to the newly opened Prince Edward MRT Station on the Circle Line via a link bridge. It is also within walking distance of the Tanjong Pagar (East-West Line) and Cantonment (Circle Line) MRT stations.

Located in District 2 at the edge of the CBD, Newport Plaza is the first freehold mixed-use project developed under URA’s CBD Incentive Scheme, which encourages the conversion of older office buildings into mixed-use developments within the CBD.

Through the scheme, the site’s plot ratio was increased, along with a 25% uplift in gross floor area to about 655,000 sq ft.

‘Urban hill’

Judges for the EPEA 2026 were impressed by the thoughtful integration of Newport Plaza’s various uses. “Balancing so many different components in a single tower is a complicated task — one that the design team manages deftly,” says Mark Ong, group director at architectural and engineering firm P&T Consultants, who sat on the judging panel this year.

Newport Plaza was designed by Japanese practice Nikken Sekkei, in collaboration with local firm ADDP Architects.

Based in Tokyo, Nikken Sekkei is a historic firm best known for designing iconic structures such as the Tokyo Skytree broadcasting and observation tower and the Tokyo Dome indoor stadium. It is also known for its extensive experience in innovative urban design, having worked on local and international projects that range from cutting-edge skyscrapers to large-scale regeneration projects.

For Newport Plaza, Nikken Sekkei’s design was inspired by the concept of an “urban hill”, according to CDL. Using biophilic design principles, the Japanese firm conceived the tower’s distinct design, featuring cascading green terraces that curve along the lower floors occupied by the offices.

More greenery is woven throughout the building through multiple sky gardens, landscaped amenity decks and a roof garden. These collectively create a “green ribbon” that visually spirals up the tower.

EPEA judge Ong commends the development’s effective use of landscaping to delineate the tower’s different uses. For example, a sky terrace at Level 10 separates the offices from the serviced apartments, while another sky terrace at Level 22 acts as a divider between the serviced apartments and residences.

The softscaped open areas at the terraces provide physical partitions between the tower’s sections, while also ensuring users of each component have “their own green spaces”, Ong points out.

Newport Plaza is the second project Nikken Sekkei has designed for CDL. The  firm also worked on Zyon Grand , a 706-unit condo by CDL and Mitsui

Fudosan on Kim Seng Road. The 99-year leasehold project also garnered multiple wins at this year’s EPEA.

Premium living experience

Newport Residences was designed to set a new benchmark for city living. Located on the tower’s higher floors, the units enjoy unblocked panoramic views of the sea and city skyline.

Apartments range from one-bedroom units starting from 431 sq ft to four-bedroom premium units of 2,067 sq ft. There is also a super penthouse on the 45th floor. Spanning 12,060 sq ft, the lavish residence includes a dedicated lift and two private carpark lots.

All units feature elegant interiors, with marble flooring in the living spaces and glass balustrades at the balconies for uninterrupted views. The living area is equipped with a Haiku-branded fan, while a grille at the main entrance allows residents to keep the door open, promoting natural airflow.

The homes come with Liebherr and V-Zug kitchen appliances, along with bathroom fittings from Dornbracht and Duravit. Larger units include additional appliances such as steamers, wine chillers and dishwashers.

The apartments also feature a smart home setup that enables devices including air conditioners, doorbells, lighting and digital locksets to be remotely controlled.

Ample facilities across multiple levels

Residents will have access to a comprehensive range of facilities, which are dispersed across six levels.

A major highlight is Newport Sky, which crowns the 45-storey tower. The roof garden takes up the entire top floor, offering residents 360-degree scenic vistas. It also features resort-style amenities including four swimming pools, a pool deck and outdoor shower, a lounge, spaces for entertaining and a concierge desk.

A full-floor amenities deck at Level 34, known as Club Vista, serves as another hub for socialising and gathering. It includes a gym, co-working area and urban farming garden, alongside gourmet and social lounges.

More amenities are available at smaller sky gardens on Levels 25, 29, 37 and 41. These include an outdoor fitness station, a playground, a yoga area and an additional co-working lounge.

All the shared spaces feature lush greenery designed by Ecoplan Asia, the project’s landscape architect.

Recalibrating strategy

Newport Residences’ Marketing Excellence title at the EPEA is special recognition for the marketing efforts for the project.

The postponed sales launch meant that the project’s marketing had to undergo a “strategic recalibration”, according to the developer. Pre-marketing activities began in early November 2025, ahead of the project’s preview and sales launch in January 2026.

Animated EDMs (electronic direct mail) were used to tease the upcoming debut, while a multi-pronged marketing strategy using print, digital and broadcast media was deployed to further build awareness and communicate the project’s key features.

To showcase the homes and Newport Residences’ facilities, the developer rolled out virtual tours, 3D floorplans and detailed renderings, which were also made available on the project’s website.

For the super penthouse, CDL went the extra mile by creating a “spacewalk” virtual tour with interactive displays within a dedicated zone at the sales gallery, allowing for a hyper-immersive experience of the luxurious residence.

The rest of the sales gallery exhibits the same attention to detail. Visitors are greeted by a reception area that leads to a soaring model of Newport Plaza. Standing about 5m tall, it serves as a focal point that reinforces the project’s scale and positioning.

A smaller secondary model, along with comprehensive mock-ups of Newport Sky and Club Vista, lets visitors see the homes and amenities more closely.  In addition, the gallery houses the showflats for the two-bedroom premium and four-bedroom premium units.

Through meticulous marketing, Newport Residences has established itself as one of this year’s standout CCR launches. With its strong performance, iconic design and compelling attributes, it comes as no surprise that the development was one of the biggest winners at this year’s EPEA.

title: Lentor Modern earns dual honours for homes rooted in nature and heritage
article:
The first and only integrated development in the immediate Lentor area, Lentor Modern brings together urban convenience and a design that pays tribute to the site’s natural heritage.

The residential component — comprising 605 homes spread across three 25-storey towers — obtained its temporary occupation permit at the end of August 2025.

Beneath the residential towers is a 96,000 sq ft commercial podium housing an integrated retail mall, which opened in January this year and is directly accessible to residents by lift.

Anchor tenants at the suburban mall include Cold Storage Fresh and Mulberry Learning pre-school, alongside a range of lifestyle, dining and essential-service options.

Lentor Modern is integrated with Lentor MRT Station, giving residents direct access to destinations such as Orchard Road, the Singapore Botanic Gardens, the CBD, Marina Bay and Gardens by the Bay.

The 99-year leasehold development by GuocoLand was the first to launch in the Lentor Hills estate. It drew a strong response, with an 84% take-up rate during its September 2022 launch weekend. It sold out in less than 2.5 years, with the last available unit sold in January 2025.

At the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026, the completed development clinched two accolades: Landscape Excellence, which recognises its strong emphasis on nature; as well as Top Development.

Integrating nature into design

Designed by ADDP Architects, Lentor Modern pays homage to the site’s heritage as a secondary forest. Nature-inspired prints adorn the retail podium’s façade, while abundant foliage and trees frame the development.

Above the podium, three residential towers rise from a landscaped deck, where a 200m meandering water feature recalls the Lentor stream that once flowed through the area.

The towers’ façades feature contrasting earth tones that complement the landscaping below.

Water and greenery are woven into the development’s recreational spaces, which include a 50m lap pool, 25m leisure pool, spa pool and jacuzzi alcove. Designed by landscape architecture firm Ortus Design, the landscape incorporates 150 species of native plants across the development.

Beyond the pools, the nature-inspired facilities include garden pavilions, a grand lawn, a glamping terrace, a full-size tennis court and a mini golf course.

The emphasis on nature continues upwards, with each residential tower featuring its own sky terrace. The verdant spaces offer sweeping views of Lower Seletar Reservoir and the surrounding landed housing enclave.

“As a condo located in the historic Lentor area, the project has done a good job of creating an ambience that feels natural,” says Ng Sze Oun, director of landscape studio Compound Collaborative and an EPEA 2026 judge.

The development is also close to nature and recreational amenities, including the future Lentor Hillock Park, Lower Peirce Reservoir Park, Thomson Nature Park and Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, with park connectors and cycling paths linking the surrounding green spaces.

Modern, comfortable homes

Practicality and long-term liveability underpin the design of Lentor Modern’s homes, which span one- to four-bedroom layouts measuring between 527 and 1,528 sq ft. These cater to diverse household needs, from young professionals to multigenerational families.

A flex room is included in the two- to four-bedders, offering homeowners a versatile space that can be used as a study, hobby room, nursery, wardrobe extension or storeroom as their needs change. Most flex rooms come with windows for natural airflow.

Everyday comfort is prioritised throughout the apartments. Windows are incorporated into the kitchens and both the master and common bathrooms, keeping spaces well-ventilated, naturally lit and comfortable for daily use.

Convenience is also built into the homes, with each unit equipped with a wireless smart home gateway system for remote control of lighting and air conditioning.

Anchoring Lentor’s transformation

Lentor Modern kickstarted the transformation of the Lentor Hills estate and anchors the new residential precinct.

The estate has seen the introduction of several other residential projects following Lentor Modern’s launch in 2022.

These include a number of GuocoLand-linked projects, such as Lentor Hills Residences , a 598-unit development launched in July 2023; and the 533-unit Lentor Mansion , which followed in March 2024.

Lentor Central Residences , a 477-unit project developed by a consortium comprising Hong Leong Holdings , GuocoLand and CSC Land , was launched in March 2025.

More recently, a GuocoLand-led consortium set a new benchmark for land rates in Lentor. In March, the consortium was awarded a Government Land Sale plot at Lentor Central for $657.1 million, or nearly $1,278 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr). GuocoLand intends to develop the site into three residential towers with up to 562 units.

The land rate beats the previous high of $1,204 psf ppr that GuocoLand paid for Lentor Modern’s site in 2021.

title: Vela Bay charts the course for Bayshore's seafront homes with coastal vistas, yacht-inspired design
article:
Bayshore is a new residential neighbourhood still taking shape along Singapore’s eastern coast.

Yet Vela Bay , the first private residential launch in the precinct, has set out to show what a new standard of seafront living in Singapore’s east could look like.

As the inaugural development in an emerging precinct, it had a unique opportunity to shape the district’s identity.

That vision guided every part of the project, from its nautical-inspired architecture to a resort-like setting that embraces the coast.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The result earned it the Top Development title at this year’s EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) and made it Bayshore’s first waterfront showpiece.

SingHaiyi Group Ltd and Chuan Capital jointly developed the 515-unit luxury project along Bayshore Walk, launching it in April 2026.

It is a rare offering in Singapore’s housing market, pairing the tranquillity of coastal living with convenient access to the city and established schools.

A strong start

Buyers responded quickly. Nearly 8,000 people visited over the preview weekend, and the project drew about 1,000 expressions of interest ahead of the launch. By the end of the launch weekend, 371 units, or 72% of the development, had been sold.

SingHaiyi put this partly down to pent-up demand. New private launches in the immediate East Coast area have been relatively limited, and the last major one nearby was Seaside Residences in 2017.

Interest came from investors, HDB upgraders and right-sizers, as well as families hoping to live closer to their loved ones.

Today’s buyers are also more discerning and look beyond location to connectivity, layouts and the overall quality of the living environment, SingHaiyi says.

Entering an emerging residential precinct as a first mover was a calculated decision.

The East Coast is already a well-established and highly sought-after residential neighbourhood, close to East Coast Park , reputable schools and lifestyle amenities, while Bayshore MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line links it directly to the city.

Rather than simply being the first to enter the market, the developers wanted Vela Bay to establish a benchmark for architectural excellence, thoughtful design and quality living that would remain relevant as the wider Bayshore community takes shape.

Designed around coastal living

More than 70% of the homes are sea-facing, with selected units enjoying uninterrupted views towards the coastline.

Working with architect P&T Consultants, the developers studied the site’s orientation to capture those views while keeping privacy, natural ventilation, solar exposure and residential density in balance. The towers are positioned so that many units avoid the harsh afternoon sun from the west.

One of the key challenges was the site’s proximity to underground MRT infrastructure and railway reserves, which constrained where buildings and facilities could go.

To work around this, the design team created an elevated bermed landscape deck that integrates essential infrastructure and servicing areas into the terrain, so residents get a raised, resort-like level set apart from the street below.

In Latin, vela means “sail”, and the condo’s design thus takes its cues from the elegance of luxury yachts gliding over calm waters and the movement of the sea.

The two towers are drawn in sleek horizontal lines, while their curved balcony edges and façade detailing recall the rhythm of ocean waves.

Sculpted rooftop crowns form a distinctive architectural silhouette and are expected to make the development a recognisable landmark along the East Coast Parkway.

At the heart of the landscape is the Vela Pavilion, a striking sail-inspired tensile canopy that serves as a focal point for the development. It is complemented by a swimming pool designed to resemble the bow of a yacht.

Inside, Singapore-based interior design studio Sujonohun created two schemes inspired by the Mediterranean Riviera.

Most units follow the “ Portofino ” concept, styled after sun-drenched seafront homes, with earthy tones and warm timber set against textured stone-look finishes.

The private lift units and penthouses use “Monaco”, a cooler palette of misty greys and ocean blues with metallic accents and refined stone textures for a sophisticated look. These larger homes also come with higher specifications, including gunmetal-finished fittings in selected bathrooms, integrated wine chillers and upgraded kitchen appliances.

Vela Bay’s units range from 484 sq ft one-bedroom-plus-study apartments to 1,582 sq ft, five-bedroom homes, along with two penthouses of 1,765 sq ft each. Two- and three-bedders make up the bulk, while larger units cater to multigenerational families.

A neighbourhood in the making

Much of Vela Bay’s long-term appeal rests on what Bayshore will become.

SingHaiyi sees it poised to emerge as one of Singapore’s most exciting new waterfront residential neighbourhoods, supported by a comprehensive master plan that brings together homes, green spaces, transport infrastructure and community amenities.

The precinct is planned as a car-lite neighbourhood with pedestrian-friendly streets and cycling paths.

The Thomson-East Coast Line is set to extend towards Changi Airport, and a mixed-use development integrated with Bedok South MRT Station and a bus interchange is on the way, along with a new Safra Bayshore clubhouse.

The developers have taken a similarly long-term approach at Vela Bay, where sustainability and adaptability are central to the design.

The development is designed to achieve BCA Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification, complemented by energy-efficient features, solar panels and building design strategies aimed at reducing environmental impact.

Its vision of urban coastal living centres on seamlessly integrating work, family, wellness and recreation into everyday life.

A resident might begin the morning with a run or cycle along East Coast Park before taking the MRT to the CBD or Marina Bay for work, then return in the evening to unwind by the yacht-inspired pool.

Weekends bring opportunities to explore the Park Connector Network and Round Island Route, with more sports and recreational facilities to come at the future Safra Bayshore clubhouse.

The ultimate objective, SingHaiyi says, is a living environment where residents do not have to choose between the convenience of city life and the restorative qualities of nature.

title: The Sen scores with award-winning design centred around wellness
article:
The site of The Sen , a 347-unit residential development in District 21, offers something rare amid Singapore’s urban setting: a sense of calm, rooted in its proximity to nature.

Located along Jalan Jurong Kechil, off Upper Bukit Timah Road , the plot is a stone’s throw from Bukit Batok Nature Park and close to Bukit Timah Nature Reserve. Other parks, such as the Rail Corridor and Rifle Range Nature Park, are also nearby.

The area’s verdant greenery has heavily influenced The Sen’s design. Drawing inspiration from the surrounding landscapes, the condo is centred around wellness principles and a connection to nature.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The result impressed judges of this year’s EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA), who conferred the development the Design Excellence title for residential non-Central projects.

The Sen is developed by Sustained Land in a joint venture with Ho Lee Group and Greatview Development. The 99-year leasehold condo occupies a 207,156 sq ft site that the partners purchased in 2024 through a Government Land Sale tender for $278.9 million, or $841 psf per plot ratio.

Seamless integration

AGA Architects was appointed to design the project. The Singapore-based practice has also collaborated with Sustained Land on previous developments, such as the 250-unit Tre Residences on Geylang East Avenue 1, the  144-unit Coastline Residences on Amber Road, and the 96-unit 3 Cuscaden on Cuscaden Walk.

With The Sen, AGA Architects had to take into account the site’s topography, which features undulating terrain.

While this could have posed a design challenge, the firm, together with landscape architect Ecoplan Asia, took advantage of the site’s natural qualities to develop the condo’s layout and configuration.

The bulk of The Sen’s facilities lie at the heart of the site, tucked centrally among the development’s five residential blocks. They are spread across two main levels: Level 1 includes the drop-off area and the clubhouse, while Level 2 features the main pool deck with a 50m lap pool.

Meanwhile, the landscaping incorporates cascading terraces and tiered plantings that provide a fluid transition between the various spaces.

A wide variety of plants and trees, coupled with water features and sculptural elements, further blur boundaries while also giving the development a resort-like feel.

The seamless integration of all of The Sen’s components stood out to Mark Ong, group director of architectural and engineering firm P&T Consultants and one of the EPEA 2026 judges.

“What was impressive about The Sen is how the design makes you ‘forget’ about the challenge posed by the site’s topography,” he says. “The project effectively weaves together amenities and other facilities while navigating the site’s different levels with ease.”

Designed for well-being

The Sen’s residential towers each span 10 storeys, with the blocks strategically oriented to maximise light and ventilation.

Their façades’ finishes emulate wood and stone, complementing the greenery of the landscaping and surrounding nature reserves.

The earthy tones were deliberately paired with the development’s multiple pools to create a tranquil environment that promotes well-being.

The philosophy extends to The Sen’s residences, which prioritise both form and function to optimise day-to-day living.

Each unit features full-length windows and a private balcony. Coupled with an open-plan layout, these allow the homes to receive ample daylight and natural airflow, which offer benefits for both physical and mental health.

Interior finishes utilise different materials, such as engineered timber flooring and large- format tiles, to offer a clean, timeless aesthetic.

Units at The Sen are categorised into Classic and Prestige. The Classic homes, which span three of the five residential blocks, comprise one- to three-bedders ranging from 452 to 1,109 sq ft.

The remaining two blocks house Prestige homes, which consist of larger three-bedroom-plus-study and four-bedroom-plus-study units measuring between 1,259 and 1,453 sq ft.

Elevating everyday living

Facilities at The Sen were curated for a holistic lifestyle, with a variety of spaces for activity, relaxation and socialising.

In addition to the 50m lap pool, residents have access to a family pool, children’s pool, tennis court, gym, steam room, and hot and cold bath.

Lounge rooms and a barbecue pavilion provide spaces for gatherings, while family-friendly amenities include a playground, a play pavilion and several open lawns. In addition, there is a childcare centre on-site, located near the entrance with its own drop-off point.

More facilities are available at three sky terraces located at the Classic blocks. The landscaped communal spaces include dedicated yoga and Pilates areas, gardens and additional spaces for entertaining.

Beyond the lifestyle amenities, The Sen integrates green features that promote sustainability and an eco -conscious lifestyle.

Solar panels on the roof will generate electricity for common areas, while each home will come with a ceiling fan in the living room, reducing reliance on air conditioning. There will also be electric- vehicle charging stations at the car park, along with bicycle facilities.

The Sen was launched for sale in November 2025, with the developers moving about 23% of its units during the launch weekend at an average price of $2,358 psf.

Caveats lodged as at Oct 15 show that over half of the apartments have been taken up.

title: Boutique hotel on Hongkong Street for sale at $32 mil
article:
A boutique hotel housed in a conservation shophouse at 41 Hongkong Street is up for sale via an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The 30-room property has a guide price of $32 million.

The shophouse is a five-storey conserved property with a six-storey rear extension on a 2,072 sq ft commercial site. The hotel — Luma41 – has 30 rooms on Levels 2 to 6, while the ground floor is occupied by Peranakan restaurant City PeraMakan.

The hotel has “80% to 90% occupancy”, according to Steward Asia (a unit of PropNex), which is marketing the property. It has also recently secured a permanent hotel license.

The shophouse has a total built-up area of approximately 8,872 sq ft, including the ground-floor F&B space of 1,051 sq ft. Based on the total built up area, the guide price works out to $3,607 psf.

Excluding the F&B component, the price for the hotel works out to “below $1 million per key”, adds Steward Asia.

The lease on the land has been topped up to a fresh 99 years from December 2018, while renovations costing $6 million have been carried out on the property, including the installation of a lift. The works were completed in 2019.

The property is a five-minute walk from Clarke Quay MRT Station.

Previously, the shophouse at 41 Hongkong Street was put up for sale for $35 million in 2023 . At the time, the hotel operated under the name Hotel Nuve Elements.

“Hotel licences in shophouses are hard to come by, and permanent ones even more so,” says Loyalle Chin, co-founder of Steward Asia. “41 Hongkong Street lets an investor step into a running hotel with its own F&B frontage, in a river precinct the government is actively revitalising.”

“With a permanent hotel licence, established operations and a prime location a short walk from Clarke Quay MRT Station, 41 Hongkong Street offers investors a rare combination of hospitality and F&B income at an attractive entry point,” adds Raelyn Lee, listing manager of Steward Asia.

The EOI closes at 3pm on Nov 27.

title: CapitaLand Investment Share Price: Why Isn’t This Stock Worth More?
article:
CapitaLand Investment Limited
(SGX: 9CI), or CLI, manages S$128 billion in
real estate
for other investors across Asia and beyond.
However, its share price just closed at S$2.40, about 25% below its 52-week high, and slightly under CLI’s book value.
So, has the market got CLI wrong, or is it right to be careful?
The short answer is that CLI looks undervalued, but the discount won’t close until it proves what its non-core assets are worth. Here’s why.
Understanding CLI’s Business Model
CLI isn’t a real estate developer.
Instead, it mainly manages capital from third parties through listed
real estate investment trusts
(REITs) such as
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust
(SGX: C38U), as well as private funds and its Ascott serviced residences, while charging fees for doing so.
It also owns stakes in those REITs and funds, plus some properties outright.
The plan since its 2021 listing has been to lean more on fees, which don’t require CLI to own every building.
Earning more from the same capital should lift returns, and fund managers usually trade at richer valuations than landlords for exactly that reason.
CLI is also squeezing more out of each dollar it manages, with fund management fees making up an increasingly large slice of CLI’s money-making pie.
Why Has CLI’s Share Price Struggled?
Property-related stocks in general have been out of favour.
Higher interest rates compress the valuations of buildings while simultaneously making it more expensive to service the massive loans taken to purchase the properties at previously higher valuations.
Hence, investors have swung away from property-related stocks, and CLI’s sell-off could be partially explained by these factors.
Within CLI itself, China remains the group’s largest drag.
Revaluation losses, mostly from China, came to S$439 million in 2025.
That cut total profit for the year by 70% to S$145 million, even as operating profit rose 6%.
Selling older assets has also taken time.
Management says S$7 billion to S$9 billion of value sits in non-core investments, most of it in China.
Investors tend to discount assets that may be hard to sell at book value.
Then, there’s complexity.
CLI mixes fund management, lodging, and direct property ownership, which makes it hard to value as one business.
Holding companies
like this often trade at a discount.
Are CLI’s Financial Results Improving?
On the surface, things are picking up.
CLI earned S$687 million in fees in the six months to 30 June 2026, 20% more than a year earlier, and that helped lift operating profit by 13% to S$293 million.
Total profit came in strong at S$327 million, with no big revaluation losses this time.
Fundraising rose 42% to S$3.7 billion, while funds under management edged up to S$128 billion.
The quality of that growth is mixed, though.
One-off transaction fees from its listed funds jumped to S$66 million from S$4 million, accounting for over half of the increase in fee revenue.
Management has already guided for deal activity to slow from first-half levels.
Cash generation also remains thin.
Operating cash flow was S$448 million in 1H2026, while S$599 million went out in dividends, causing cash on hand to fall to S$1.58 billion from S$2.02 billion.
That said, the balance sheet is in decent shape: the net debt/equity ratio is 0.45 times, the interest coverage ratio is a healthy 4.3 times, and the average borrowing cost is just 3.5%.
Is CapitaLand Investment Trading Below Its True Value?
CLI’s latest net asset value (NAV) stands at S$2.50 as at 30 June 2026.
Given that its share price has been around S$2.40, CLI is trading slightly below book value.
A small discount to book value alone doesn’t mean that shares are undervalued.
Here’s a simple way to see why the shares look cheap.
Add up what CLI says its stakes are worth, about S$17.2 billion, with nearly half of that in listed REITs, then subtract S$6.1 billion of net debt.
You’re left with roughly S$11.1 billion.
The whole company is valued at about S$12.0 billion on the stock market.
The catch is that those investment values are CLI’s own book figures, and many REITs trade below their book values.
If the China assets sell below book value, the upside is smaller than it looks.
In other words, investors are paying very little for the fee business, which earned S$495 million in EBITDA over the 12 months to 30 June 2026.
Applying a fair multiple of 15x to these earnings shows the upside once investors start giving CLI credit for its fee-earning business.
What Could Unlock Value for Shareholders?
Selling non-core assets near or above book value would do the most.
CLI has made about S$5 billion of gross divestments so far in 2026, listed a China REIT and is aiming for a second by the end of 2026.
Faster fee growth would also help.
CLI is targeting S$200 billion of funds under management by 2028.
A stronger showing in its lodging segment would be helpful as well.
Then there are capital returns.
CLI has paid an S$0.12-per-share core dividend every year since 2021, representing a 5.0% yield at today’s price.
Management says surplus capital will go back to shareholders, but CLI bought back no shares in 1H2026.
With the share price below book value, buybacks would arguably do more than higher dividends.
What Could Keep the Share Price Depressed?
A weaker property market, especially in China, would mean more write-downs.
Fee growth could slow once one-off deal fees fade.
Selling assets at a discount or taking on more debt would also hurt.
Without a clear catalyst, a cheap stock can stay cheap for years.
Get Smart: A Hidden Bargain or a Justified Discount?
CLI looks undervalued.
With shares trading slightly below book value, investors get a growing fee business for free, plus a 5.0% dividend yield while they wait.
The discount isn’t irrational, though.
China exposure, uneven fees and a complex business structure that is harder to value explain much of it.
The catalyst to watch is non-core asset sales.
If CLI keeps selling at close to or above book value and hands the cash back to shareholders, the market will have little reason to keep the discount.
For patient investors, it’s worth a closer look.

title: Cyberattackers drain money from French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea
article:
(Nov 4): Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said hackers stole money from it after gaining access to its computer systems, underscoring the growing cybersecurity risks for the banking sector.

The French lender “was the victim of a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions to be carried out”, a spokesperson confirmed to Bloomberg News on Wednesday (Nov 4), declining to say how much money was stolen.

The spokesperson said some transactions have been suspended and the bank is in contact with authorities about the attack. The situation is “under control", and there will not be a financial hit to clients.

It is the latest example of cyberattacks on banks around the world. The State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender by assets, recently launched a probe after a suspected cyberattack exposed thousands of customer records containing personal information. In Japan, a wave of data breaches has hit companies including Daiwa Securities Group Inc, East Japan Railway Co and SoftBank Corp, prompting government officials to step up cybersecurity measures.

Hackers also recently pulled off the biggest heist that the digital-asset industry has ever faced, draining more than US$6 billion from crypto exchange Binance.

Cyber risks are increasing “exponentially” and represent “the price to be paid for all this innovation", UBS Group AG CEO Sergio Ermotti said earlier this week. Good governance, clear accountability and the ability to react quickly in this environment are key, he added.

See also: Singtel, DART launch cyber training with simulated attacks on critical infrastructure networks

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa earlier this year filed an application to obtain a MiCA authorisation, the European regulation on crypto-assets, to offer crypto services to its customers.

title: India approves US$1.5 bil push for energy storage capacity
article:
(Nov 4): India will set aside INR145 billion in subsidies to help build 92GWh of energy storage capacity, seeking to make better use of its rapidly expanding renewable power fleet and transmission network, information minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters in New Delhi on Wednesday (Nov 4).

The financial boost will run through 2031 and is designed to help companies in the storage sector kickstart operations as the nascent market takes off.

Currently, India’s storage capacity sits at about 54GWh but the government aims to reach 411GWh of storage capacity by the financial year 2031-32.

The decision seeks to address a growing structural challenge for India’s energy transition, as the country has been adding more solar and wind generation capacity than the grid is able to absorb. Solar and wind capacity has quadrupled since 2017 to about 230GW, accounting for 41% of the total installations. Billions of dollars have also been invested in transmission lines to carry renewable electricity across the country.

But much of that infrastructure cannot be fully utilised around the clock. Solar plants stop generating after sunset while during the day the grid can struggle to absorb all the electricity produced when solar output peaks.

The subsidies are meant to lead to a total investment of INR976 billion and will require companies applying for support to source at least 40% of their equipment in the country, encouraging domestic manufacturing.

See also: Singaporean plan to import clean power hits Indonesian hurdle

The cabinet also approved financial incentives worth over INR28 billion to bolster processing of critical minerals in the country, Vaishnaw said. The move will boost India’s manufacturing in sectors including electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence and heavy equipment and will help the country reduce import dependence, she told reporters.

title: Thai spyware alerts prompt opposition leaders to demand probe
article:
(Nov 4): Two Thai opposition leaders are demanding the government disclose whether state agencies targeted political leaders with spyware ahead of a December no-confidence debate, days after Apple Inc software flagged attempted attacks on their phones.

Opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut of the People’s Party and Democrat Party leader Abhisit Vejjajiva said at a joint press conference on Wednesday that they’d received mobile security alerts, raising questions over whether the alleged attempted intrusions may be linked to their scrutiny of the government.

Abhisit called on the government to confirm that no security agency or other state body was involved in the incidents, which triggered the phone alerts late in October.

The government has already denied targeting politicians with spyware, and Digital Economy and Society Minister Chaichanok Chidchob on Tuesday said that similar alerts were reported across 99 countries. He said authorities were seeking information from Apple Inc and planned to raise the issue at the National Security Council.

His deputy, Boonthida Somchai, said affected politicians had not yet submitted their alerts directly to the ministry for verification.

Former MP Wiroj Lakkhanaadisorn, an ex-chair of the House Armed Forces Committee, told Bloomberg that attempts to extract information from another person’s phone could constitute a criminal offence.

See also: Indonesia arrests ex-police chief for alleged wiretap of Prabowo

He argued that such surveillance would violate Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act and called for answers from the government, including Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in his capacity as head of the Internal Security Operations Command, citing past allegations involving the agency. ISOC is the internal security arm of the Thai armed forces.

The lawmakers’ questions come the same week that Germany’s government confirmed that Bundestag members had received Apple alerts about apparent spyware attacks.

Wiroj said preparations for the Dec 7–11 no-confidence debate remain secure but urged an investigation into possible interference in parliamentary scrutiny. He suggested referring the matter to the current chair of the House’s Committee on the Armed Forces, arguing that Apple’s security warnings warranted investigation.

title: Global renewable stocks surge after democrats sweep congress
article:
(Nov 4): Renewable energy stocks rallied around the world after the Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, an outcome seen as supporting more favourable policy for the industry.

Denmark’s Orsted A/S, an operator of offshore wind farms, was the biggest gainer in Europe, rising as much as 8.1%, with Vestas Wind Systems A/S and SMA Solar Technology AG among others climbing.

In US premarket trading, First Solar Inc advanced as much as 9.2% and Sunrun Inc added as much as 9.4%.

That followed similar gains in Asia: South Korea’s Hanwha Solutions Corp surged 19%, while HD Hyundai Energy Solutions Co and OCI Holdings Co jumped 12% and 10% respectively.

According to Barclays plc analysts, the midterm results ease political risk on US renewables and supporting networks.

“It potentially reduces the risk of further political interference with renewable energy incentives and provides greater protection for the long-term economics of US wind, solar and battery storage investments,” the analysts led by Peter Crampton wrote in a research note.

See also: Saudi budget deficit more than doubles on war, Aramco fees

“This should help ease investor concerns around regulatory uncertainty, support confidence in future project returns and potentially drive a reduction in the risk premium applied to US renewable assets."

Investors see a Democratic wave as supportive of companies in the clean energy supply chain, including solar and batteries, at the expense of the traditional energy sector. Renewable stocks are also benefiting from a rotation away from artificial intelligence-related stocks.

“The blue trade is showing up already with money rotating out of the AI buildout and into what a Democratic Congress favours," said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. Hanwha Solutions “benefits directly if a Democratic Congress pushes back on Trump’s anti-solar policy” as its Qcells business operates big US factories, she added.

See also: Eurozone 3Q growth beats estimates despite slump in France

JPMorgan Chase & Co strategists had said ahead of the midterms that a “blue wave” would be encouraging for clean-energy stocks through greater support on appropriations, oversight and permitting.

title: Eurozone wage growth to slow sharply next year in boost for ECB
article:
(Nov 4): Euro-area pay growth is poised to slow sharply in the third quarter of 2027, encouraging news for the European Central Bank as it battles inflation driven by the Iran war.

The ECB’s wage tracker, published Wednesday (Nov 4), predicts salaries will rise by an annual 2.4% between July and September next year. That’s below the forecast of 2.8% for the first and second quarters. All readings are far below 2024’s 5.3% peak.

Policymakers are particularly attentive to pay developments at present as they aim to stop energy-driven inflation from becoming entrenched through wages and firms boosting prices. Inflation expectations among euro-area households increased slightly again in September.

The ECB kept interest rates unchanged last week following quarter-point hikes in June and September. But officials are ready to raise again next month if the inflation outlook doesn’t improve.

Wages don’t show a material response at this stage, the ECB said last week. But it listed the possibility of stronger-than-expected pay increases as one factor contributing to upside risks to the outlook. Some officials argue the ECB cannot just wait for such outcomes to materialise, as acting only at that stage could be too late.

title: Singapore proposes arrests, hefty fines to toughen haze law
article:
(Nov 4): Singapore’s government has proposed amendments to toughen its law on cross-border haze, responding to a devastating wildfire season in Indonesia that cloaked the city-state in smog for weeks.

The country is seeking to bolster existing rules with measures including restrictions and fines for businesses dealing with entities or individuals suspected to have engaged in conduct leading to the blazes, Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu said.

The changes would also allow for arrests in Singapore and would boost the maximum fines for causing or contributing to haze-related fires from $100,000 per day to $1 million per day, with the cap increasing tenfold to $20 million.

“Following the recent haze episode, it is clear that the status quo is not tenable,” Fu said in a Parliament session on Wednesday. “We need better ways to obtain and verify information, trace complex corporate relationships and impose meaningful consequences on errant entities, even where criminal prosecution proves difficult.”

Fires in Indonesia have spewed pollution across the region in recent months, sending air quality to “very unhealthy” levels at times in Singapore. The smog — which has also fuelled protests in Indonesia — has spread into Malaysia and the Philippines, closing schools and driving demand for air purifiers.

The enhanced legislation is Singapore’s latest effort to hold firms accountable for the seasonal fires, which are often linked to land clearing for agriculture. The issue has been worsened this year by a strong El Niño weather pattern that exacerbated and prolonged the dry season. Rains have recently picked up, improving air quality levels.

See also: Indonesia rain set to ease toxic haze in Singapore, Malaysia

The latest amendments will allow for offences to be heard in court in the absence of an accused person, and expand the scope of the act to include conduct contributing to land and forest fires that pose a risk of haze pollution to Singapore — even before it reaches its shores.

“The punishments are not only monetary. The measures can be used to restrict and deny commercial activities and financing — effectively making the company a corporate pariah,” said Simon Tay, chairman of the Singapore Institute of International Affairs, an independent think tank. “There are nevertheless safeguards to ensure that prevention, proof and punishment will be administered justly in accordance with the rule of law.”

Singapore enacted its transboundary haze law in 2014, allowing the country to issue daily fines to polluting companies. The city-state tried to enforce that legislation during a severe haze episode in 2015, but conceded at the time it was having difficulty getting information from Indonesian authorities. Several cases remain under investigation.

See also: RegCo issues additional queries to SGX-listed companies with links to haze

The government recently stepped up efforts to pursue companies that may have contributed to this year’s pollution. The amendments would allow for greater ability to conduct such investigations.

The National Environment Agency has issued notices to a number of firms in Indonesia and separately sought information from 10 Singapore-registered palm oil and forestry companies, including Wilmar International Ltd, Golden Agri International Pte Ltd, and First Resources Ltd.

Senior government officials also met representatives of the Singapore-based companies issued notices by NEA, saying they would be expected to appoint independent assessors to examine their operations, supply chains and corporate relationships. Fu said last week the government would amend the haze law to give the framework legal force.

The number of hotspots detected in Indonesia in September and October were the highest since 2015, the forestry ministry’s SiPongi platform shows.

While advances in satellite imagery and modelling have improved authorities’ ability to trace smoke, Singapore still needs official information and records from host countries where the fires occur to pinpoint those responsible, Fu said in a parliament session on Tuesday.

She added that Singapore has offered firefighting and cloud-seeding assistance, while stressing that any support must be coordinated with Jakarta. Indonesia informed Singapore last month that it was able to handle the fires and didn’t require foreign assistance, she said.

“We don’t want to offer help when they don’t need or impose ourselves,” Fu said, adding that Singapore would continue discussions with Indonesian counterparts on how it could complement their efforts.

The two countries signed an environmental cooperation agreement in June that includes transboundary pollution, while Singapore is also working through Asean toward the region’s goal of being haze-free by 2030 as it prepares to chair the association next year.
